task: Use the actual television receiving antenna in Figure 127 to judge the incident wave's magnetic-induction oscillation direction. Separate what the drawing establishes from added assumptions about the wave, propagation direction and antenna/polarization matching. Do not replace this with an unconditional vertical-B answer or a figure-free general transverse-wave principle.
figure_facts_used: The actually opened original PNG and current complete modern preview show an upper approximately horizontal crossbar carried by an upright/supports over a roof, with a visible descending/bent line and three separated lower stroke groups.

The drawing has no incident-wave arrow, transmitter bearing/elevation, E/B vectors, polarization labels or statement of maximized polarization coupling. Vertical supports/roof strokes are not drawn B vectors.

The near-horizontal upper crossbar supplies the antenna axis needed for an explicitly assumed ideal electric-dipole receiving model. Its physical horizontal interpretation and idealization are stated when applying that model; a page projection does not independently supply a three-dimensional wave direction.
Complete right/bottom content is visible. These observations are for solving this task only, not a renewed image/source-fidelity audit.

independent_solution.zh: 只凭图127的天线外观，不能唯一确定电视台来波的磁感应强度矢量B的实际振动方向，也不能无条件说B竖直。图可识别上部近水平接收横杆，但没有给出传播方向、线偏振状态或接收天线是否与入射极化完全匹配。若把横杆作为理想电偶极子接收元件，接收电压取决于E在其有效长度方向的投影；非零接收并不推出E只沿横杆。对于均匀各向同性介质中的远场平面电磁波，E与B均横于传播方向，并有B=(khat叉乘E)/v。因此，若另行假设线偏振远场波、横杆为物理水平方向且与E的极化方向匹配，则E沿该横杆，B在垂直于横杆的平面内；这仍不必竖直。再加来波水平传播且垂直于横杆，才推出B沿竖直轴来回振动。竖直结论属于该组假设，不属于原图单独必然给出的事实。图示天线的水平轴、接收E投影/极化匹配和传播方向须共同参与解释，不能只复述E、B、k互相垂直。
independent_solution.en: Figure 127 alone does not uniquely determine the incident magnetic-induction vector's actual oscillation direction, and does not justify unconditional vertical B. The upper approximately horizontal receiving crossbar identifies an antenna axis, but no propagation direction, linear polarization or perfect polarization match is specified. In an explicitly assumed ideal electric-dipole receiving model, induced voltage depends on the projection of E onto effective antenna length; nonzero reception does not imply that E is exclusively along the rod. For a far-field plane electromagnetic wave in a homogeneous isotropic medium, E and B are transverse to propagation and B=(khat cross E)/v. If one additionally assumes a linearly polarized wave, a physically horizontal dipole rod and matched E polarization along it, B lies in the plane perpendicular to that rod, not necessarily vertically. If the incident wave also propagates horizontally perpendicular to the rod, B oscillates along the vertical axis. That vertical result is conditional, not a fact proved by the drawing alone. The original task requires the figure's rod axis, electric-field projection/polarization matching and wave direction to be related, not only a generic perpendicular-fields slogan.

truth_basis.authority: Allowed q4 seed prose, actual original/current figure observations, ideal electric-dipole projection and plane-wave vector relation; no author agreement or previous answer/key used.
truth_basis.coordinate_convention: x along the assumed physical horizontal receiving rod; z vertical; y the other horizontal axis; right-handed coordinates.
truth_basis.receiving_model: V_oc is proportional to h_eff dot E; for an ideal rod h_eff is along x. A nonzero x projection does not require zero y/z components.
truth_basis.plane_wave_model: B=(khat cross E)/v, with positive wave speed v; khat dot E=khat dot B=E dot B=0. A fixed oscillation axis additionally requires linear polarization.
truth_basis.unconditional_from_figure: No unique actual B oscillation direction. Antenna appearance alone does not determine the incident polarization/propagation.
truth_basis.matched_rod_conditional: For a linearly polarized plane wave with E parallel to x, B is perpendicular to x, in the yz plane. The plane is not a single vertical direction.
truth_basis.vertical_B_conditional: With matched E along x and horizontal propagation khat along y, B is proportional to -z; sign reverses during oscillation, so the oscillation axis is vertical.

counterexamples.name: matched_rod_but_elevated_wave
counterexamples.purpose: Perfect rod/E polarization matching by itself allows inclined B when propagation is inclined.

counterexamples.name: horizontal_incidence_but_nonexclusive_E
counterexamples.purpose: Horizontal incidence and nonzero reception do not alone force vertical B; full polarization matching is a separate assumption.

counterexamples.name: matched_rod_vertical_incidence
counterexamples.purpose: A second admissible geometry gives horizontal rather than vertical B with the same matched rod.
